title: An AI Oracle's Rise and Fall
summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner, a former OpenAI researcher once hailed as a visionary and dubbed the "Nostradamus of AI," saw his hedge fund unravel just two days before his wedding after it had grown to manage $45 billion in assets. Wall Street now views the episode as a cautionary tale about an inexperienced investor taking on outsized risk on AI-driven investment theses.

title: Nvidia Wants to Run the World's Robots. China Is an Eager Customer.
summary: Nvidia is pushing to power a growing wave of humanoid and industrial robots, and Chinese manufacturers are emerging as enthusiastic buyers of its chips and software for what the industry calls "physical AI." Trade in this category remains open under current U.S. export rules, even as Washington restricts other categories of AI hardware sales to China.

title: How Big Tech Blinded Itself to the Grassroots AI Revolt
summary: Wall Street Journal reporting describes how major technology companies have become caught in their own echo chamber, causing their established AI strategy playbook to falter against a grassroots backlash. The piece argues the industry misjudged how quickly public and developer sentiment could turn against its approach to deploying AI.

title: SoftBank in Talks to Buy Majority Stake in Humanoid Maker 1X at $6 Billion Valuation
summary: SoftBank is in talks to acquire a majority stake in humanoid robot maker 1X at a $6 billion valuation, marking another robotics bet by founder Masayoshi Son. 1X, which has backing from OpenAI, has yet to prove its technology works reliably at commercial scale.

title: Meta Reaches $18 Billion Settlement Over Child Safety Claims
summary: Meta Platforms agreed to an $18 billion settlement with a coalition of 48 states that had accused the company of misleading the public about the safety of Instagram and Facebook and contributing to child addiction to its apps. The company will make annual payments over the next decade and must limit users under 18 to two hours of daily use while blocking overnight feed scrolling within six months. Meta said it would pay the full amount only if TikTok and YouTube adopt similar daily time limits and matching payments; New Mexico had already won its own case against Meta, while Florida declined to join the settlement.

title: Employers Are Making Job Candidates Jump Through Hoops to Prove They're Real
summary: Amid rising AI-enabled cheating, deepfakes, and fraudulent remote workers, employers are adopting new interview screening tactics such as asking candidates to remove Zoom backgrounds or pan cameras around a room. The trend reflects growing employer concern about verifying that job candidates are who they claim to be and possess the skills they represent.

title: How Salesforce Is Overhauling the Way It Charges for AI
summary: Salesforce is shifting how it charges for its Agentforce AI product, moving away from pure subscription pricing toward models tied to usage and outcomes. The company is negotiating custom contracts that charge businesses based on how much the AI grows revenue by helping close deals or cuts costs by automating customer service interactions, illustrating a broader software-industry shift toward outcome-based AI pricing.

title: How Apple Stumbled Into AI Hardware Success With the Mac
summary: Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio computers have become unexpectedly popular, driven by demand from users running AI agents and developers training and running AI models locally to cut cloud computing costs. Mac sales grew nearly 29% year-over-year to $10.4 billion in the June quarter, outpacing every other Apple product segment.

title: McKinsey's 2026 State of AI
summary: McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey of 1,719 respondents across 97 countries found that 40% of large organizations (over $1 billion in revenue) now report scaling AI agents, up from 27% a year earlier, and about 31% of larger organizations are scaling software coding agents. Eighty percent of respondents said AI has improved their individual productivity, but only 37% attributed any EBIT impact to AI use, roughly flat from the prior year, pointing to a persistent gap between individual productivity gains and measurable business impact.

title: From Enterprise AI POC to P&L
summary: McKinsey published guidance on moving enterprise AI initiatives from proof-of-concept to measurable production impact, drawing on engagements with a global manufacturer and a large conglomerate scaling agentic AI. The firm argues the gap between AI's promise and production reality comes down to delivery practices rather than better models, citing redesigned workflows, measuring impact in P&L terms rather than accuracy, and dedicated production AI engineering staff as key differentiators.

title: Nvidia Reportedly Agrees to Buy Hugging Face for $12.9 Billion
summary: Nvidia is reportedly acquiring open-source model repository Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, as interest in open-source AI models continues to grow following gains by Chinese model developers. The deal would give Nvidia a significant stake in the infrastructure underlying open-source AI model distribution.

title: Tim Cook Hands Over Apple CEO Role to John Ternus
summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO after 15 years, with John Ternus succeeding him effective August 31; Cook becomes executive chair focused on policy engagement. Apple's annual revenue grew to an expected $477.7 billion from $108 billion when Cook took over in fiscal 2011, though Ternus inherits a maturing iPhone market and looming competition from OpenAI's planned AI-native devices.

title: Shein Set to Debut on Hong Kong Exchange at Sharply Reduced Valuation
summary: Fast-fashion retailer Shein is expected to go public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange this week at a valuation of roughly $26 billion, far below the $98 billion it reached in a 2022 funding round. The company's disclosures show its U.S. business shrank in the first quarter after the closure of a duty-free import loophole for low-value packages.

title: The $5.5 Billion Perk SoftBank's Data-Center Venture Offered to Land OpenAI
summary: SoftBank's data-center unit, SB Energy, offered OpenAI a $5.5 billion incentive as part of an agreement deepening the financial ties between the two companies on AI infrastructure projects. The arrangement underscores SoftBank's aggressive push to lock in OpenAI as a long-term partner in its data-center buildout.

title: Ernst & Young Is Giving $100 Million in Bonuses to Staff for 'Human' Skills
summary: Ernst & Young is distributing $100 million in bonuses to employees who demonstrate strong critical thinking, judgment and other traits the firm considers essential to working effectively alongside AI. The move is part of a broader push among professional-services firms to cultivate skills that complement, rather than compete with, AI tools.

title: What CEOs Can Learn From the AI Backlash
summary: In a WSJ Leadership Institute interview, columnist Tim Higgins explains how an insular Silicon Valley culture and a shift toward bypassing traditional media left tech leaders such as Meta and OpenAI blindsided by a grassroots backlash against AI data centers. The piece argues the backlash will intensify heading into the November midterms alongside Anthropic's expected IPO, though it notes Microsoft's longer-established government-relations operation has helped it navigate the moment more smoothly than peers.

title: Anthropic Considers Letting Shareholders Sell In IPO, Departing from SpaceX Playbook
summary: Anthropic is weighing a plan to let some existing shareholders sell stock as part of a potential IPO, a departure from the lockup approach SpaceX has used in its own share sales. The AI company is also reportedly considering a longer-than-usual lockup period following any public listing.

title: Inside Cognition's Booming Growth, High Cash Burn
summary: AI coding startup Cognition's annualized revenue has tripled this year to reach $900 million, even as its cash burn is on pace to hit as much as $800 million. The figures illustrate the steep costs AI coding companies are absorbing to sustain rapid growth.

title: Why CoreWeave Is The Best Neocloud Buy
summary: The Information's analysis argues CoreWeave trades at a valuation discount to rival AI-cloud providers Nebius and Iren, even when measured against 2028 projected revenue, making it an attractive buy among the so-called neocloud operators. The piece frames the comparison as a reason investors may be undervaluing CoreWeave relative to its growth trajectory.

title: China's CXMT Makes Breakthrough in Advanced Memory Chips
summary: Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT has begun producing HBM3E, an advanced high-bandwidth memory chip, a development that could help accelerate China's efforts to build domestic AI processors. The breakthrough narrows the technology gap between CXMT and established memory suppliers like Samsung and SK Hynix.

title: Musk Responds to Report About SpaceX Setting Up a Turbine Blade Factory
summary: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX is laying groundwork for in-house casting of turbine vanes and blades, saying the move could accelerate natural-gas turbine deployment by up to 18 months to address a looming AI data-center power shortage. Musk cited an estimate that 15 gigawatts of AI chips due next year won't be able to come online because of power and equipment shortages, a supply crunch worth hundreds of billions of dollars in idle hardware.

title: OpenAI Pulls Its AI Models From SpaceX-Owned Cursor
summary: OpenAI said it will terminate its contract to supply AI models to coding assistant Cursor by November 12, following Cursor's $60 billion acquisition by Elon Musk's SpaceX, citing distrust stemming from past conduct by Musk-owned entities. Cursor said OpenAI accounts for only about 5% of its traffic and that it generates roughly $4 billion in annualized revenue overall, while Anthropic said it would continue supplying Claude models to the platform.

title: Andreessen Horowitz Raises $1.1 Billion for AI Hardware Fund
summary: Andreessen Horowitz raised $1.1 billion for a new fund dedicated to physical AI and infrastructure startups, including companies building chips, memory, networking and storage for the AI buildout. The raise comes about nine months after the firm closed a $15 billion fundraising round that included $1.7 billion earmarked for AI infrastructure investments.

title: PayPal Falls 12% After Stripe and Advent End Pursuit
summary: PayPal shares fell 12% after Bloomberg reported that Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International had dropped their pursuit of acquiring the company. The shares fell to $54, below the roughly $60.50-per-share offer the consortium had made in July, which would have valued PayPal above $53 billion and which PayPal had viewed as insufficient.

title: Kalshi Court Setback Raises Prospect of Supreme Court Fight
summary: A federal appeals court ruled that states have the right to regulate prediction markets, dealing a setback to Kalshi and increasing the likelihood the company will seek Supreme Court review. The Ninth Circuit's decision, which upheld a Nevada gambling injunction against Kalshi, conflicts with an April Third Circuit ruling that found Kalshi's sports-event contracts were federally regulated swaps.

title: China's CXMT Sues the U.S. for Inclusion on Military-linked Blacklist
summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's leading memory chipmaker, is suing the U.S. Department of Defense in an effort to be removed from a Pentagon blacklist of Chinese military-linked entities. The company, added to the list in January 2025 and retained after a June 2026 review, denies any military affiliation and joins a growing number of Chinese firms, including Alibaba, that have challenged similar designations in court.

title: Nvidia's $3.5B MediaTek Bet Reveals Its Plan for Tackling Big Tech's AI Chip Buildout
summary: Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek through convertible bonds, deepening a partnership spanning AI data-center infrastructure, PCs and automotive platforms. The deal gives MediaTek access to Nvidia's NVLink Fusion ecosystem to help design custom AI chips for hyperscalers, a move seen as Nvidia's strategy to stay central to AI infrastructure even as major cloud providers build their own chips.

title: Consumer Cellular to Add 120 Stores by Year-End
summary: Consumer Cellular is on track to reach 120 retail stores by the end of 2026, having already grown from 83 stores across 30 states earlier in the year to 100 stores across 33 states by mid-year. The company says retail locations accounted for 14.4% of new customer accounts so far this year, more than double the 6.3% share a year earlier, as it bets on physical stores while some rivals shift online.

title: Samsung Locks Up 70% of Memory Chip Supply Through 2031
summary: Samsung has committed roughly 70% of its memory-chip production capacity to long-term agreements running through 2031 with customers including Microsoft, Google and Nvidia. Long-term contract pricing for HBM3E runs four to five times cheaper than the spot market, a reallocation of capacity toward AI-focused memory that is expected to tighten supply and keep prices elevated broadly.
